rationale: I read the complete held EO 12291 (46 FR 13193, Feb. 17, 1981, 'Federal Regulation'): definitions, regulatory impact analysis and OMB review, agendas, the Task Force on Regulatory Relief, pending-regulation provisions (sec. 7), exemptions, judicial-review disclaimer (sec. 9) and sec. 10 revoking EO 12044 and 12174. It has no own sunset and no savings clause. I read the held text of EO 12866 (58 FR 51735, Sept. 30, 1993) around its secs. 9-11: sec. 11 'Revocations. Executive Orders Nos. 12291 and 12498; all amendments to those Executive orders; all guidelines issued under those orders; and any exemptions from those orders heretofore granted for any category of rule are revoked.' That is an express, unqualified revocation of the whole order naming it by number, with no delayed effect, carve-out or savings language, and EO 12866 sec. 9-10 contain only a no-displacement-of-agency-authority and judicial-review disclaimer. The other machine-found acting instruments (EO 12319, 12371, 12482, 12492, 12495, 12621, 12637) are amendments or exemptions that left EO 12291 in force and are not an ending; EO 12498, 12612 and 12803 are 'See:' cross-references. The catalog note ('Revoked by: EO 12866, September 30, 1993') and the 1989 snapshot row ('Codified at Chapter 34, p. 702', i.e. still in the 1989 codification, consistent with a later 1993 revocation) are leads only; the basis is the held acting text. Later orders that reworked EO 12866 do not revive EO 12291. Earlier endings: none found in the held record; none would change a NO. Provisional NO hypothesis only; first-effective date (signing Sept. 30, 1993 vs publication Oct. 4, 1993) is not asserted.
